title: Potato (Solanum tuberosum)
description: Global comparative analysis of potato cultivation strategies across different climate zones.
overview: The potato is a starchy root vegetable native to the Americas. It is one of the world's most critical staple crops. However, due to its sensitivity to high temperatures and water stress, cultivation strategies vary wildly depending on the regional climate.

regions.challenge: Heavy summer monsoon rains cause massive fungal infections (Late Blight) and tuber rotting if planted in summer.
regions.strategy: Avoid the monsoon. Potatoes are planted in early spring (March) and harvested before the monsoon begins in late June. Alternatively, they are grown in autumn after the rains stop, or in high-altitude alpine regions (Gangwon Province) during summer where it remains cool and well-drained.

key_metrics.irrigation_need: Low to Moderate (Rain-fed mostly, avoiding monsoon)
key_metrics.primary_disease: Phytophthora infestans (Late Blight) driven by high humidity

regions.challenge: Increasingly hot and dry summers due to continental climate shifts, leading to water stress and secondary growth (knobby tubers).
regions.strategy: Planted in mid-April and harvested in September. Because summers lack the heavy monsoon of Korea but suffer from drought, supplementary overhead irrigation is absolutely critical during the tuber bulking phase (July-August) to maintain consistent soil moisture and prevent malformed potatoes.

key_metrics.primary_disease: Colorado Potato Beetle (Leptinotarsa decemlineata) and drought-induced physiological defects
